name: AI Battle vs 1v1 PvP Isolation & Popup Audit
note: Two things this gate holds down. The AI match loop was moved out of battleService so a practice match cannot touch the PvP transport — that isolation is structural and has to stay that way. And battle.css leans on a CSS Grid Stack to keep card height identical across thirteen languages, which is invisible in the CSS itself and only survives while it is written down. The second mutation edits a file in ../../app_common, which the harness restores by content hash like any other; note that the run's `git status` cross-check only covers this repository, so that one file is verified by hash alone.

mutations.name: the AI session reaches back into the PvP service
mutations.why: A bot match that imports battleService can write to a real matchmaking room. The player practising against a bot then shows up in someone else's live game.
mutations.replace:
import { aiBotService } from '../engine/aiBotService.js';
import { battleService } from './battleService.js';

mutations.name: the layout standard stops naming the property the CSS depends on
mutations.why: `grid-area: 1 / 1` in battle.css looks like dead styling. It is the whole Grid Stack pattern: every option's description is stacked in one cell so the browser measures the longest one in the ACTIVE language and the container stops shifting height when the player switches chips. Somebody rewriting the standard without naming the property leaves the CSS looking removable, and the next person removes it — after which German and Spanish start moving the buttons under the card. The rule and the code have to fall together.
mutations.expectFailure: must document the Grid Stack pattern

mutations.name: a human opponent with AI in their name is taken for the bot again
mutations.why: 2026-10-21: a real player is named Player_ + the last four characters of their id, so about one opponent in 1,200 has AI or bot in the name. Guessed from the name, their rematch started an AI battle and closing the result went to the AI screen.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] a human opponent named Player_kAIz is not taken for the bot

mutations.name: the AI test reads the isAIBattle field nothing sets
mutations.why: The field the six places read first. Nothing ever set it, so AI rooms were found only by the bot’s English name — read alone, every AI battle is a 1v1 on screen.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] an AI room (classic) is taken for an AI battle

mutations.name: the battle header guesses from the name again
mutations.why: The header’s AI tag and icon came from the bot’s English name. Translating the names (D28) would have shown PVP on every AI battle.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] src/components/BattleHeader.jsx decides an AI battle with isAIRoom

mutations.name: the back button reads the never-set field
mutations.why: Leaving an AI battle with the back button sent the player to the 1v1 lobby whenever the name did not say AI.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] src/hooks/useBackStack.js does not decide an AI battle

mutations.name: a new name guess appears somewhere else in src
mutations.why: The six were copies of one expression. A seventh written the old way anywhere in the app brings the misfire back.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] nothing in src guesses the bot from the opponent

mutations.name: the AI room carries an English name again
mutations.why: D28 (2026-10-22): AI Grandmaster and the rest were English in all thirteen languages.

mutations.name: an AI room is no longer named by its bot
mutations.why: Without the id the name falls back to one title for every bot.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] an AI room is named by its bot id

mutations.name: the battle header names the opponent its own way again
mutations.why: Two screens naming the opponent two ways is how the header and the result card come to disagree.

mutations.name: a German bot name says AI instead of KI
mutations.why: The German review settled on KI (DE29-12); a bot named AI beside the KI tag reads as untranslated.

mutations.name: a duel win that unlocked something does not hold the rematch banner
mutations.why: D32 restored: Play Games draws its achievement popup over the top of the screen for about five seconds, and a rematch asked for then puts its banner underneath — who is asking and how long is left cannot be read.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] a duel win that unlocked something starts the hold

mutations.name: the hold is dropped every render
mutations.why: The first D32, restored: the held request was cleared in the subscription effect's cleanup, which App re-runs on every render (a new startNewGame each time) — so no held banner ever showed. Only the two-phone test caught it.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] the subscription effect's cleanup does not drop a held request

mutations.name: the asker's countdown is stopped every render
mutations.why: D33 restored: the subscription effect's cleanup cleared the asker's interval, and App re-runs that effect on every render — the button showed 「신청 중... (15s)」 and never counted (Velvet, 2026-10-22). It came back only when the other side's banner timed out and declined.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] the subscription effect's cleanup does not stop the asker's countdown

mutations.name: a held banner starts from a fresh 15 seconds
mutations.why: The asker's own countdown kept running while the banner was held; a banner that starts again from 15 can accept after the asker's button came back, into a match they had given up waiting for.
mutations.find: return { waitMs, seconds: Math.max(1, REMATCH_SECONDS - Math.ceil(waitMs / 1000)) };

mutations.name: the hold is shorter than the popup
mutations.why: Measured on the Flip5: 5.1 s from the unlock to the popup leaving. A three-second hold puts the banner up while the popup still covers it — the bug, two seconds later.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] the hold covers the popup as measured

mutations.name: the banner ignores the seconds it was given
mutations.why: The timing is worked out in the hook and handed down; a banner that always starts from 15 undoes it where the player can see it.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] and the banner counts down from them

mutations.name: a forfeit win reads as finishing first
mutations.why: BT-3: without its own sentence the result card tells a player who won because the other side left that they completed the puzzle first.
mutations.expectFailure: [FAIL] the result card explains a win by forfeit
